title: Bind bounded deterministic recovery and lifecycle ownership
recovery_contract: pid birth is taken from the process probe and a reused pid is not the same worker
process generation and lease generation must both match the durable lifecycle
a stale claim is released without disturbing a live owner
a dead worker is fenced and its generation advances only when effects are known
an idle runnable queue wakes only after its deadline and does not mask a dead worker
unknown effects stay unknown and block requeue and rebind
holds and deadlines admit no lifecycle mutation
the durable recover budget is the campaign limit of 2 and a checkpoint cannot refund it
limitations: Recovery decides lifecycle ownership. It does not signal processes, start systemd units, call a provider, or write native task status.
An unknown effect stays unknown. Recovery will not mark it applied, requeue its task, or bind a replacement worker over that generation.

The recover budget is DEFAULT_LIMITS['recover'] from the WWL-100 progress ledger, which is 2. A bound ledger with any other recover limit is refused. Noise, retries, and checkpoints do not refund a spent incident.
A hold or a deadline that has already arrived records the refusal and leaves generations, claims, effects, and the runnable queue unchanged.
